title: Connectives
subtitle: Time phrases, although, despite, however and unless

blocks.text: With some time words and phrases, we use the present simple to talk about the future. We don't use **will** or **be going to**.

rows.example: I'll call you **after** we **solve** the problem.
I'll call you **as soon as** we **solve** the problem.
It'll be a few days **before** we **find** the solution.
I won't call you **until** we **find** the solution.
It'll be great **when** we **find** the solution.
I'll be in the office **while** I **deal** with this problem.

blocks.text: We can also put these time words and phrases at the beginning of the sentence.
blocks.note: **As soon as** we solve the problem, I'll call you.

blocks.text: We use the word **although** to express contrast. Form: **Although** + subject + verb, subject + verb

rows.example: **Although** my homework was difficult, I finished it before bed.

blocks.text: We can also put **although** in the middle of the sentence.
blocks.note: I finished my homework before bed, **although** it was difficult.

blocks.text: We use **in spite of** and **despite** to express contrast. They mean the same thing.

rows.use: In spite of / despite + -ing form, subject + verb
rows.example: **In spite of revising** for hours, I didn't do well in the test.

rows.use: In spite of / despite + noun, subject + verb
rows.example: **Despite my revision**, I didn't do well in the test.

blocks.text: We can also put **in spite of** and **despite** in the middle of the sentence.
blocks.note: I didn't do well in the test, **despite** revising for hours.

blocks.text: We use **however** to express contrast. Form: Subject + verb. **However**, subject + verb.

rows.example: We believed that we would find a solution. **However**, we were wrong.

blocks.text: We can also put **however** at the end of the second sentence.
blocks.note: We believed that we would find a solution. We were wrong, **however**.

blocks.text: The word **unless** means **if … not** or **except if**.

items: **Unless** you hurry up, we'll be late. (= If you **don't** hurry up, we'll be late.)
For more information about conditional sentences, see Units 28 and 29.

exercises.title: A · Time clauses
exercises.instruction: The phrases in bold are wrong. Write the correct phrases.

items.prompt: We'll have something to eat when we **will get** home.
I won't book the tickets until you **will tell** me to.
I'll come home as soon as the concert **will finish**.
acceptedAnswers: as soon as the concert finishes

items.prompt: After you **are going to do** this test, we'll play a game.
He'll send you a text message before he **is going to leave**.
Will you go to St. Petersburg while you **will be** in Russia?

exercises.title: B · Verb box
exercises.instruction: Complete using the correct form of the verbs in the box.

items.prompt: Call me as soon as you ___ any news.
She'll have to do a lot of revision before she ___ the exam.
Are they going to visit you while they ___ in the UK?
Do you want to go to university after you ___ school?
Claire won't have a break until she ___ all her homework.
The lesson can't start till the teacher ___ .
___ the water was cold, we still went swimming.
___ my mum's got a mobile, she never uses it.
___ looking for hours, I couldn't find a nice pair of jeans.
___ taking a map, we still got lost.
I don't like sweets, ___ I do like chocolate.
We enjoyed the picnic ___ the bad weather.
___ it was expensive, the CD wasn't very good quality.
___ being expensive, the CD wasn't very good quality.
___ the cost, the CD wasn't very good quality.
The CD was expensive. ___ , it wasn't very good quality.
The CD was expensive. It wasn't very good quality, ___ .
The CD wasn't very good quality, ___ being expensive.
The CD wasn't very good quality, ___ it was expensive.
The CD wasn't very good quality, ___ the cost.

exercises.title: E · unless
exercises.instruction: Complete each second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence.

items.prompt:
If the traffic isn't bad, she'll be here at six o'clock.
Unless the traffic ___ bad, she'll be here at six o'clock.
acceptedAnswers: Unless the traffic is bad, she'll be here at six o'clock.

items.prompt:
If it doesn't rain, we'll go to the beach.
Unless it ___ , we'll go to the beach.
acceptedAnswers: Unless it rains, we'll go to the beach.

items.prompt:
If I'm not tired, I'll come to the party.
Unless ___ tired, I'll come to the party.
acceptedAnswers: Unless I'm tired, I'll come to the party.
Unless I am tired, I'll come to the party.

items.prompt:
If Mrs Potts doesn't come, we won't have a test.
Unless Mrs Potts ___ , we won't have a test.
acceptedAnswers: Unless Mrs Potts comes, we won't have a test.

items.prompt:
If Sarah comes, we'll watch the video.
We'll watch the video unless Sarah ___ .
acceptedAnswers: We'll watch the video unless Sarah doesn't come.

items.prompt:
If Mum gives me some pocket money, I'll buy a new pair of jeans.
I won't buy a new pair of jeans unless Mum ___ some pocket money.
acceptedAnswers: I won't buy a new pair of jeans unless Mum gives me some pocket money.

exercises.title: F · One door leads to freedom

items.prompt: (1) ___ you choose the right door, you can go free.
(2) ___ , if you choose the wrong door, you have to stay in prison forever!
And it gets worse! (3) ___ one of the guards always tells the truth, the other one always lies.
It's an impossible situation — isn't it? No, it's not. But (4) ___ you're extremely careful, you might choose the wrong door.
And you shouldn't choose a door (5) ___ you're absolutely sure it's the door to freedom.
And you'll only know it's the right door (6) ___ you ask the right question.
(7) ___ of not knowing if the guard always tells the truth or always lies, you'll always get an answer that will help you.
(8) ___ you get the answer, go through the other door. You'll be free!
